correctness.rationale: From the established wedge theorem, Alexander duality concentrates H^1 of the connected dual and supplies the ambient permutation-sign tensor factor. The dual faces are exactly sets with at most one nonneighbor per vertex. For a reflection, the two-mirror-pair compatibility criterion is proved as b=min(x+y,n-x-y)<=p using n>4p; the signed invariant-family involutions near vertex and edge axes leave contributions p and p-1, with a further +1 from two fixed vertices. This gives the three displayed reflection values. Prior rotation character and exact averaging give all dihedral quotient ranks. Independent direct dual and original complex tests covered 90 reflection actions, six original-cut checks, 21 full-group quotients, and five exact mod-two H1 ranks. These tests support, but do not replace, the universal proof.

value.rationale: The two reflection conjugacy classes are geometrically natural but not determined by the established C_n-module for cycle-power three-cut complexes. Their exact characters complete an infinite-family D_n homology representation, and the quotient Betti theorem exhibits a sharp and interpretable n mod 4 transition including infinitely many rationally acyclic quotients. This is a structural fixed-face localization contribution, not a narrow arbitrary table or routine restatement of previous sphere ranks.
